title: Monotone feedback does not generally maximize mean productive function
statement: For integrable output laws, all bounded increasing sensors preserve G>=H expectation iff G first-order stochastically dominates H. Higher mean alone is insufficient, and identical observable laws cannot identify differing external utility.

body: Necessity follows by using increasing threshold indicators at each cutoff. Sufficiency follows by approximating bounded increasing functions by nonnegative sums of such indicators (and passing to integrable limits as appropriate). A higher mean permits crossing survival curves, so a threshold sensor can reverse that ranking. If all observables have identical laws for two programmes, any policy based only on them has identical information and cannot infer their different unobserved utility. A reproductive count is appropriate for reproductive utility only under actual genotype/function coupling.
